How to bounce back
from a terrible week
Sleep first. Before you fix anything, get one full night of rest. Problems look half as big after eight hours of sleep, and your decisions get twice as good.
Clean one space. Your room, your desk, your car. Restoring order in one small area gives your mind a feeling of control when everything else feels messy.
Move your body hard once. A run, a swim, a heavy workout. Physical effort burns off the stress chemicals a bad week leaves behind in your body and mind.
Talk to one person you trust. Not to complain for hours, just to share it. Saying out loud what went wrong often makes it feel lighter and much clearer.
Before: bad weeks dragged into bad months. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a daily moment of curiosity that pulls my head out of the stress.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: bad weeks dragged into bad months. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. A daily moment of curiosity pulls me out of the stress.

slides.texte_overlay: Write down three lessons. What happened, what you'd do differently, what was out of your control. A bad week becomes useful the moment you learn from it.
Plan one small win for Monday. A task you can finish by ten. Starting the new week with a quick success breaks the spell of the old one and gives you momentum.
